step_by_step_reasoning:
1. External users/clients interact with individual Client S3 buckets (indicated by the incoming arrow on the left).
2. Access logs from all Client S3 buckets are delivered to a dedicated S3 Access Logs bucket.
3. The landing of access logs in the S3 Access Logs bucket triggers an AWS Lambda function.
4. Lambda parses logs, converts IP addresses into numeric country IDs, appends client metadata, and indexes the records into Amazon Elasticsearch Service (OpenSearch).
5. Anomaly detection running within Elasticsearch detects unusual access patterns and triggers an alert via Amazon SNS.

graph.name: Mobilewala - Real-Time Anomaly Detection using Amazon Elasticsearch Service
graph.notes: Mobilewala uses Amazon Elasticsearch Service's anomaly detection feature to analyze S3 access logs in near real-time, sending alerts via SNS when suspicious access patterns are detected.
